source_note: Curated from ASML's 2022 company retrospective. These are attributed historical statements, not inferred causal links or an exhaustive independent history.

milestones.title: Kinoshita's early EUV imaging work
milestones.description: ASML's retrospective attributes early EUV image projection and a 1986 presentation to Hiroo Kinoshita at NTT.

milestones.title: US national-laboratory EUV research
milestones.description: The retrospective describes Hawryluk's work and subsequent DOE support for US laboratory research; this is not evidence that all US work descended from a single Japanese paper.

milestones.title: First Dutch EUV images
milestones.description: ASML's retrospective dates Fred Bijkerk's first Dutch EUV images to 1990.

milestones.title: EUV LLC and the Virtual National Laboratories
milestones.description: Industry-supported laboratory research helped move EUV toward industrialization. The year is an approximate program milestone.

milestones.title: ASML forms EUCLIDES with European partners
milestones.description: ASML, ZEISS, and Oxford Instruments formed EUCLIDES; the retrospective also identifies Dutch and German research partners.

milestones.title: EUCLIDES and EUV LLC join forces
milestones.description: ASML dates the collaboration between the European consortium and American EUV LLC to 1999. Japan pursued ASET and later EUVA programs in parallel.

milestones.title: ASML ships EUV prototypes
milestones.description: Prototype systems went to imec in Belgium and SUNY in New York, where researchers studied EUV process integration.

milestones.title: First TWINSCAN NXE:3100 shipment
milestones.description: ASML shipped a pre-production EUV system to Samsung in South Korea.
